author: /root
body:
# Task 2.2 bounded JSON job transport

Outcome: additive internal transport for complete JSON job/history objects, not a native artifact schema or semantic connection. The measured informed pair is 9.20 MB canonical ASCII JSON; a generic postorder interned JSON DAG is 7.93 MB without opening authored chunks. Avoid special-casing any theorem, history, or profile.

APIs: pack_json(value, *, limits=TransportLimits()) -> bytes; unpack_json(raw, *, limits=TransportLimits()) -> dict. New module ladon.bounded_json_transport and private helpers permitted. Closed wire schema ladon-bounded-json-dag-v1 with schema/root/nodes/expandedBytes/digest. Nodes tagged scalar/object/array, object keys sorted unique and refs strictly backward true ints. Root is final object node. Canonical ASCII JSON, no duplicate keys/nonfinite numbers; preserve integer/float distinction, finite floats, Unicode, negatives and integers above2^53. Duplicate rows, unreachable nodes, noncanonical ordering/encoding, forged size/digest and malformed tags/refs must reject. Reconstruct independent mutable containers at repeated references, not aliased Python owners.

Fixed maximum profile: wire8MiB; expanded canonical ASCII JSON32MiB; depth272 (root depth0); scalar/key UTF8 bytes1MiB; DAGnodes100000; DAGedges500000; expanded value occurrences1000000. Configured limits may narrow, never enlarge these maxima; true positive ints only. The expanded32MiB is a separately specified aggregate JOB footprint consistent with existing bounded aggregate loader/Real analysis, not a relaxation of any artifact8MiB/string1MiB/native scalar schema or of process12GiB/output8MiB caps. Future consumers must still validate original native envelopes and exact owners after decoding. No authority, authenticated authorship, currentness, parsing of nested JSON strings, public command or SQLite change.

Decoder validates byte bound before JSON parsing; complete schema/topology/canonical graph and bottom-up expanded size/depth/value counts before any tree materialization. Reject exponential DAG bombs before expansion. Encoder must also preflight shared/cyclic Python structures and expanded budgets before serialization; do not traverse exponentially before checking. At most linear graph work plus bounded expanded reconstruction/canonical verification; no compressed-byte decompressor or external dependencies. Exact round trip by canonical bytes, not equality alone (1 ==1.0 is inadequate). No truncation/stubs.

Root owns production edits/shared tests/builds/board. Workers read only or isolated scratch proposals. Preserve prior dirty tree, all protected inputs and eight earlier sealed packets. Never push/commit. Freeze reviewed red tests after checking their own quality, then implement and run independent integrated audit. Per supervised qualification operation<=600s, process tree12GiB, output8MiB. Production connection/deadline/fresh admission and Task2.2 remain open until their own gates pass.

author: /root/transport_red_67
body:
Read-only falsification review of Task 2.2; no tests/builds/Lean or source edits performed. Source inspected: CONTRACT.md, FEASIBILITY.json, src/ladon/real_prose_native_codec.py, and src/ladon/real_bound_native_analysis.py::_bound_inputs. Existing history codec canonicalizes ASCII JSON and checks cycles/depth iteratively, but then uses recursive JSON parse/dump; aggregate loader serializes the full value tree and enforces 32 MiB after constructing bytes. New DAG transport must meet the contract's preflight requirement rather than inherit those allocation patterns.

Decisive red test groups:
1) Envelope/canonical input: reject >8 MiB before json.loads; duplicate wire keys at any nesting level; NaN/Infinity; UTF-8/non-ASCII wire bytes or whitespace/key-order/noncanonical escaping; unknown/missing envelope or node fields; wrong schema; digest and expandedBytes altered independently; byteLength/limits booleans (bool is an int subclass). Then require exact pack/unpack/pack bytes on valid inputs, including Unicode escaped canonical form, 1 vs 1.0, -0.0, finite floats, huge signed integer >2^53, null/bools.
2) Node grammar/topology: each tag's closed field set and scalar type; reject bool and float refs, negative/out-of-range/forward/self refs; root must be final object node; duplicate rows (including semantically duplicate scalar/container rows); unreachable nodes; duplicate/unsorted object keys; duplicate object member rows; malformed key values; arrays/object child refs with wrong shape. Valid refs to prior nodes must round trip, with deliberate deterministic node ordering.
3) Resource preflight: construct tiny high-fanout repeated-reference DAG where expanded output exceeds 32 MiB while wire is tiny; assert rejection from bottom-up DP before any materialization (can monkeypatch/guard materializer or use a sentinel allocator hook if API permits). Separately cross exact expandedBytes, depth 272/273, scalar/key UTF-8 length 1MiB/1MiB+1, nodes100k/100k+1, edges500k/500k+1, and expanded occurrences1m/1m+1; assert booleans/zero/negative/non-int/above-hard-max configured limits reject. Ensure occurrence accounting counts every expansion through repeated refs, not unique DAG nodes.
4) Ownership and encoder preflight: pack cyclic containers and reject; reject tuple/set/custom mapping, non-string keys, nonfinite floats. Shared Python list/dict referenced in two positions should encode legally, unpack into equal but non-identical containers; mutating one decoded branch must not change the other. Use a shared DAG whose expanded value/byte budget is over limit and verify encoder rejects before recursive traversal/serialization. Include deep 272/273 values without relying on Python recursion as the check.
5) End-to-end/native boundary: transport job aggregate can exceed 8 MiB but remain <=32 MiB, yet the nested native artifact/envelope still independently fails its unchanged 8 MiB, 1 MiB scalar, exact-owner/shape validators when invalid. This proves transport is not a native-schema relaxation. Do not parse JSON-looking strings as nested transport data.

Risk notes: graph uniqueness/canonicality must be specified mechanically, or several byte encodings may decode to one value and digest alone does not establish canonical representation. DP must account for JSON escaped ASCII byte lengths (not Python character length), punctuation, keys, and each repeated occurrence. Iterative graph validation can still be followed by recursive materialization and fail at Python recursion depth; keep materialization iterative and bounded. Independent mutable reconstruction may itself require work proportional to expanded output, so the 32 MiB/1m occurrence check must happen first. Preserve integer/float distinction and signed zero through canonical JSON and the DAG scalar tags.

Existing feasibility numbers are pair raw 9,197,980 bytes, DAG 7,929,606 bytes, 23,505 nodes; therefore the demonstrated 8 MiB target has only ~458 KB headroom. Include the exact pair, plus boundary variations that cross the wire limit, as non-gating evidence; do not claim these measurements validate a new encoder.

author: /root/transport_green_68
body: Encoder proposal: iterative identity-DFS over exact builtins (dict/list only), sorted dict keys, gray/black identity state; gray revisit is a cycle, black revisit is shared edge and costs O(1). For each scalar/container compute a type-sensitive structural signature (float distinct from int; float token via canonical json.dumps, preserving -0.0), hash-cons equivalent rows, and emit first-use postorder IDs. In the same postorder pass compute exact unfolded canonical ASCII subtree byte size, unfolded value-occurrence count, and subtree height. Object footprint = braces + each sorted canonical key token + colon + child footprint + commas; array = brackets + child footprints + commas. Use cap+1 saturating arithmetic at expanded byte/node ceilings to reject before any JSON serialization. Root depth is zero; reject height > max_depth. Track actual unique DAG nodes/edges and UTF-8 byte lengths of strings/keys. Avoid recursive unfold; preflight cost O(unique containers + edges), including shared/exponential structures. Then encode wire with canonical separators/ASCII/sorted header keys and check wire ceiling before returning.

author: /root/transport_green_68
body: Decoder proposal: require exact bytes and wire bound first; strict UTF-8/ASCII JSON parse with object_pairs_hook rejecting duplicate keys and parse_constant rejecting NaN/Infinity, then require canonical re-dump bytes equal input. Validate exact header keys/types (type(x) is int for all indices/counts, never bool), schema, digest format, nodes/tags/arity, sorted unique object keys and UTF8 key/scalar bounds. In one forward node pass enforce backward refs, count unique nodes/edges, derive signatures, reject structurally duplicate rows, and compute subtree bytes/occurrences/height with saturating bounded sums; check root is last object, reachable (canonical DFS from root), expected expandedBytes, and canonical SHA-256 over canonical expanded tree bytes. To prove canonical postorder IDs/order without building a tree, walk reachable DAG iteratively in canonical child order, postorder hash-cons signatures, and require the resulting unique rows/index assignment exactly matches wire nodes (rejects alternate order/orphans). Only after every check call _materialize; expand each ref occurrence into fresh list/dict recursively/iteratively, never memoizing mutable owners. Contract/RED findings: byte footprint and identity ownership are unfolded metrics while DAG size is unique graph metrics; both must be independently capped.
